title: heuristic-cost-cartography-journal
content:
Goal: exploratory journal for mapping heuristics that predict per-request inference cost under variable runtime behaviors. This is a personal scratchbook for prototype API shapes, config sketches, and a small ASCII architecture diagram to communicate the idea to the runtime team.

High-level motivation:
- We need a lightweight estimator that runs at ingress (or client) and can tag requests with a predicted cost bucket (cheap|med|expensive).
- Downstream routing, batching, and admission control can use the bucket to make routing decisions and to compute per-tenant billing signals earlier in the pipeline.
- Estimator must be robust to model variant fallbacks, KV cache hits, and sequence-length tail events.

Non-goals (for this journal):
- Exact per-token accounting (that's for billing pipeline).
- Full ML model training artifact—this is heuristic-first, ML-second.

Quick ASCII diagram (runtime ingress view):

  [CLIENT] --> [INGRESS LB] --> [PREFETCH / ESTIMATOR] --> [ROUTER] --> [SERVING RUNTIME POOL]
                                         |                       |                     |
                                         v                       v                     v
                                    [LOCAL CACHE]         [COST-ANNOTATOR]      [K/V CACHE / KV-HOTSTORE]

Notes on components:
- PREFETCH / ESTIMATOR: lightweight JS/Go service that inspects prompt metadata (prompt length, presence of tools, streaming hint) and local telemetry to output: {cost_bucket, cost_score, bias_factors}.
- LOCAL CACHE: stores recent prefix checksums -> cached_kv_hit boolean; used by estimator to reduce false expensive tags. TTL short (~2m).
- COST-ANNOTATOR: enriches traces with predicted cost and emits sample metrics for calibration.

API Shape: estimate endpoint prototype (text only, JSON payload shown as illustrative string)

Request (POST /v1/estimate-cost)
{
  "client_id": "tenant-123",
  "model_hint": "gptx-13b.q4_0",
  "prompt_tokens": 146,
  "expected_completion_max_tokens": 512,
  "system_instructions_length": 28,
  "tools_attached": ["search", "calculator"],
  "streaming": false,
  "prefill_hint": "none",
  "recent_kv_key": "sha256:abcd..."
}

Response
{
  "cost_bucket": "med",            /* cheap | med | expensive */
  "score": "0.67",               /* 0..1 confidence/score */
  "factors": "[\"long_completion\",\"tools\"]", /* as stringified list to keep top-level simple */
  "annotations": "kv_hit_expected=false;prefetchable=true"
}

Implementation sketch / DSL for routing policy using estimator output:
- routing.rulebook (example lines)
  - if cost_bucket == cheap and latency_slo < 200ms -> route: low-cost-fast-pool
  - if cost_bucket == med -> route: mixed-pool with batching window 20ms
  - if cost_bucket == expensive -> route: queued-pool + quota-check + optional model-variant-fallback

Config sample (YAML-ish as text)
estimator:
  version: v0.3-experimental
  heuristics:
    - name: token-length-slope
      weight: 0.45
    - name: tool-presence-penalty
      weight: 0.25
    - name: kv-cache-boost
      weight: -0.7
  kv_cache_ttl_secs: 120
  emit_sampling_rate: 0.02

Back-of-envelope formula (prototype):
  score = sigmoid( w_len * prompt_tokens_normalized + w_max * expected_completion_norm + w_tools * n_tools + w_kv * kv_hit_prob)
  bucket thresholds: score < 0.25 -> cheap; 0.25..0.7 -> med; >0.7 -> expensive

Calibration experiments notes (run results appended from local sim):
- dataset: 2k sampled requests from staging traffic (rand week).
- baseline naive estimator (tokens only) accuracy vs observed cost quartile: 0.58
- heuristic ensemble above (weights tuned by grid-search on staging): 0.73 accuracy
- edge cases: very short prompts + very long completions (underpredicted cost), tool chains with low completion tokens but high compute (e.g., tool: external-exec) underpredicted.

Operational considerations:
- privacy: estimator may run in client SDK optionally to avoid sending raw prompt to estimator service. But client-side heuristics will diverge and need stronger sampling/telemetry hooks.
- sampling for calibration: must attach sample_id to routed requests for later reconciliation with actual token usage.
- fallback: if estimator fails, default to med to avoid underprovisioning expensive cases.

Open design questions / TODOs:
- Q1: Should the estimator return per-token forecast distribution or only bucket? (Tradeoffs: payload size vs routing granularity)
- Q2: How to incorporate KV cache hit rate from history when the hot key is tenant-scoped vs global? (privacy + accuracy concerns)
- Q3: Can we derive an inexpensive per-tenant correction factor from recent bill cycles to adjust estimator bias?
- Q4: Is it worth shipping a tiny on-device linear model (client SDK) to improve cold-start accuracy?

Action items (owner: Maya / eng-serving-runtime):
- [ ] spike: implement Go PoC for /v1/estimate-cost and add sampling hook in ingress (2d)
- [ ] run sims on one-day production trace subset and compute confusion matrix (3d)
- [ ] draft routing-rulebook PR for runtime routing (Jon)
- [ ] define telemetry schema id and add to trace enrichment (Priya)

Notes-to-self: keep this journal terse, capture experiments inline. If this looks promising, move to a proper PRD and add a confluence page.\n
Recent thought dump (2024-11-02):
- Maybe expose an optional explain-token where estimator returns a compact bitmask of dominant heuristics (bits mean long_compl|tool|kv_miss|streaming). This keeps response tiny and actionable.
- Consider using reservoir-sampled telemetry to limit sensitive payloads while keeping calibration signal.

References / links (quick):
- Ingress sim repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ingress-sim (PR-342 for sample harness)
- Routing rulebook draft: CONFLUENCE-ENG/heuristic-cost-cartography
- Jira: ENGINF-912 (estimator spike ticket)

End of scratch journal entry.
